packages.title: Subnational electricity meter versus on-site generation QA
facts: DESNZ subnational electricity estimates are based on meter-level consumption data.
Electricity consumed directly from on-site generation is not captured in the subnational meter dataset.
Energy Trends includes some on-site generated and consumed electricity that subnational estimates exclude.
The subnational dataset is an annual consumption estimate, not a greenhouse-gas measurement.
No parcel-level emissions value is supported by these meter aggregates.

packages.title: Subnational GB versus UK scope QA
facts: The 2024 subnational electricity and weather-corrected gas report covers Great Britain.
Energy Trends comparison figures cover the United Kingdom.
Geographic scope differences can create level differences between the two sources.
GB totals cannot be relabelled as UK totals without an explicit bridge.
No parcel value is inferred from national or local-authority scope.

packages.title: Subnational weather-corrected gas QA
facts: The 2024 subnational summary reports weather-corrected gas consumption.
Weather correction changes the interpretation of year-to-year gas consumption comparisons.
Gas consumption is reported as energy use rather than CO2e.
Meter-based gas statistics have administrative classification rules.
No emissions factor is silently applied.

packages.title: Subnational domestic-meter threshold QA
facts: Gas meters above 73,200 kWh per annum are classified as non-domestic in the subnational statistics.
Smaller commercial properties can therefore be classified as domestic.
This classification can affect trends over time.
Domestic/non-domestic meter classes are not equivalent to building-use truth at parcel level.
No parcel emissions are inferred from meter class.

packages.title: Subnational versus Energy Trends alignment QA
facts: DESNZ states that subnational and Energy Trends electricity trends are broadly aligned but totals differ.
Subnational electricity excludes some on-site generation and Central Volume Allocation consumption.
Energy Trends is top-down while subnational data aggregate meter-level consumption.
Methodological differences must be preserved in comparisons.
No source is treated as interchangeable without qualification.

packages.title: Residual-fuel definition QA
facts: DESNZ residual fuels exclude gas, electricity and road transport fuels.
Residual fuels include coal, petroleum, manufactured solid fuels, bioenergy and waste.
Residual-fuel statistics are energy-consumption estimates.
They do not directly report greenhouse-gas emissions.
No parcel-level fuel use is inferred.

packages.title: Residual-fuel GIS-model QA
facts: Subnational residual-fuel estimates use GIS methods within the NAEI work programme.
Spatially resolved energy consumption estimates remain modelled estimates.
Modelled local energy use is not direct meter or parcel measurement.
Methodology vintage must be preserved.
No model result is promoted to parcel truth.

packages.title: Total-final-energy future-release guard QA
facts: The 2024 sub-national total final energy consumption release is scheduled for 30 July 2026.
At the current 25 July 2026 date that scheduled release is still future.
The announcement describes aggregation of electricity, gas, road transport and residual fuels datasets.
A future release announcement is not observed statistical data.
No unreleased value is used.

packages.title: Rail traction versus non-traction QA
facts: ORR Rail environment covers traction energy and estimated CO2e emissions.
It also includes non-traction energy, water and waste metrics.
Traction and non-traction energy must remain separate.
Environmental activity metrics are not interchangeable with emissions.
No parcel inference is made.

packages.title: Rail passenger versus freight emissions QA
facts: ORR reports passenger and freight rail emissions within the Great Britain rail environment release.
The 2024-25 total estimated rail CO2e was 2,460 kilotonnes.
Passenger and freight contributions are separately identifiable.
Rail-operator emissions are not parcel emissions.
Annual GB rail totals are not local property measurements.

packages.title: Rail passenger-kilometre intensity QA
facts: ORR reports passenger-train emissions intensity per passenger kilometre.
An intensity metric is not the same as total emissions.
Passenger-kilometre denominators must be preserved.
Intensity cannot be assigned to a parcel without activity data.
No denominator substitution is allowed.

packages.title: Rail estimated-CO2e status QA
facts: ORR describes rail CO2e as estimated emissions.
Traction electricity and diesel consumption are core activity inputs.
Estimated CO2e must not be labelled direct stack measurement.
Time-series breaks and methodology notes must be respected.
No false precision is added.

packages.title: HEE June-2026 provisional QA
facts: The June 2026 Household Energy Efficiency release is provisional.
It covers ECO and Green Deal measures and related analysis.
Provisional statistics are subject to future revision.
Installed measures are programme activity, not measured parcel GHG.
No final-status claim is made.

packages.title: HEE Table T1.6 correction QA
facts: DESNZ states Table T1.6 was corrected on 25 June 2026.
The correction followed identification of an error in the original publication.
Revision history must be retained with extracted metrics.
Earlier values must not silently overwrite corrected values.
No parcel emissions are derived from the correction.

packages.title: HEE estimated-savings QA
facts: HEE publications include estimated carbon and energy savings from installed measures.
Estimated savings are distinct from measured household energy use.
Programme savings estimates are distinct from observed parcel emissions.
Scheme coverage and geography must be preserved.
No realised-emissions claim is inferred.

packages.title: HEE detailed-report 2025 scope QA
facts: The detailed HEE report published in March 2026 covers measures and insulation levels through end-2025.
It applies across Great Britain scheme contexts described by DESNZ.
It includes ECO, Green Deal and other government support-scheme breakdowns.
Insulation level is not direct operational GHG measurement.
No parcel-level value is produced.

packages.title: HEE Great-Britain geography QA
facts: Household Energy Efficiency statistics apply to England, Scotland and Wales.
That scope is Great Britain rather than the entire United Kingdom.
Geographic coverage must be preserved when comparing with UK-wide energy or GHG data.
Scheme activity is not equivalent to all-building activity.
No local parcel extrapolation is permitted.

packages.title: CCA Target Period 7 QA
facts: The new Climate Change Agreements scheme began on 1 January 2026.
Target Period 7 runs from 1 January to 31 December 2026.
Its target-period report deadline is 1 May 2027.
A target period is a compliance framework rather than an observed emissions dataset.
No target is treated as realised emissions.

packages.title: CCA levy-reduction versus emissions QA
facts: The CCA scheme is voluntary for eligible energy-intensive industrial facilities.
Participants may qualify for reduced Climate Change Levy rates in return for meeting energy-efficiency or carbon-saving targets.
Tax treatment is not an emissions measurement.
Eligibility does not prove a facility met its target.
No parcel GHG value is inferred from CCA participation.

packages.title: CCA target versus observation QA
facts: CCA agreements set energy-efficiency or carbon-saving targets.
Targets must remain distinct from reported performance.
Performance reporting occurs after target periods.
Scheme obligations can continue from earlier phases.
No target value is recorded as observed emissions.

packages.title: CCA facility versus parcel QA
facts: CCA eligibility applies to qualifying industrial facilities and processes.
A facility boundary is not automatically a cadastral parcel boundary.
Agreement participation does not establish parcel geometry.
Scheme data must be joined only with verified facility and geometry identifiers.
No spatial inference is made.

packages.title: CCA umbrella versus underlying agreement QA
facts: CCA umbrella agreements establish sector-level frameworks.
Underlying agreements apply obligations to individual operators or facilities.
Sector and operator agreement levels must not be conflated.
Agreement templates were updated for the 2026-2030 phase.
No sector target is assigned to a parcel.

packages.title: Farm Practices Survey versus inventory QA
facts: The February 2026 Farm Practices Survey is an annual survey of farming practices.
It reports farmer responses and proportions of holdings.
It is not the UK greenhouse-gas inventory.
Survey action rates cannot be summed into national emissions totals.
No holding response is converted into parcel CO2e.

packages.title: Farm Practices Survey England scope QA
facts: The 2026 Farm Practices Survey results apply to England.
British Survey of Fertiliser Practice has a broader Great Britain framing.
England survey percentages must not be relabelled GB or UK percentages.
Geographic scope is preserved across comparisons.
No parcel extrapolation is made.
